title: Edge fleet cost & performance brief - 2026-07-06
content:
Summary:
This note captures the weekly - quick sync focused on the edge GPU fleet (APAC + EU edge zones), cost vs latency tradeoffs we observed in the past week, and planned actions to improve tail latency without materially increasing committed spend. Meeting 2026-07-06 10:00 PT, duration 45m.

Attendees:
- Aisha Raman (note owner)
- Diego Morales
- Priya Kapoor
- Samir Patel
- Ellen Wu
- Guests: Morgan Lee (SRE), Ravi Shenoy (Serving runtime)

Top-line signals this week:
- Mean request latency in APAC-edge rose from 58ms to 74ms for p50 small-chat workloads after we enabled aggressive consolidation on 5/7 node groups. p95 rose from 180ms to 260ms.
- Cost per 1M tokens served on edge zones is down ~7% week-over-week but unit latency SLO breaches increased by 12% in EU-west-edge.
- Cache hit rate for prefix cache in edge pools stayed steady at 31%, but eviction churn increased in spots by 18% (likely due to bursty onboarding of new customers).
- Prewarming pipeline (warm-images-for-gpu) succeeded for 82% of scheduled slots during the autopreheat window; failures tied to a kernel mismatch (NCCL/driver) in a small subset of older hosts.

What we discussed (high level):
1) Root cause hypothesis for latency tail in APAC-edge
   - Consolidation autoscaler policies pushed heavier density on a subset of instance types (A100-40GB mixed workload). Combined with larger sequence lengths from a new customer beta, this increased serialization on IO and longer per-request scheduling delay.
   - Evidence: host-level queuing spiked in the same time windows as p95 breaches; per-host GPU utilization averaged 87% vs expected 70%.

2) Cost/latency trades that are acceptable
   - Team consensus: keep overall unit cost improvement target for edge at -5% quarter-over-quarter, but allow a temporary +10% in region-specific burst budgets when p95 latency is >200ms for more than 2 hours. We will capture automatic fallback to Dedicated-capacity for critical tenants during those windows.

3) Prewarm reliability action items
   - Priya to open a patch for the driver/kmod alignment script and run canary on 12 hosts in apac-edge by 2026-07-09 (Linear RUN-498).
   - Samir to add an additional prewarm retry with a staggered backoff when the image fails due to kernel mismatch (ETA 2026-07-10).

4) Prefix cache experiment and short-term mitigations
   - We will increase per-host prefix cache allocation by 8% in EU-west-edge to test whether hit-rate gains reduce p95 for short chat sessions. Pilot run for 48 hours starting 2026-07-08. Owner: Diego.
   - If hit-rate improves >6 percentage points and p95 drops >15%, roll to remaining EU-edge pools.

5) Routing policy changes
   - Implement a temporary ‘latency-aware routing’ override: route requests from priority tenants to Dedicated or alternate region when edge p95 exceeds configured thresholds for >1 hour. Implementation tracked in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/721.

Monitoring and signals to watch:
- Per-host queue depth (new telemetry) - Morgan to finish dashboard by 2026-07-09.
- Cache hit rate + eviction churn per pod - alert when eviction churn > 12% for 30m.
- Prewarm failed slots per region - alert above 5% for the autopreheat window.
- Cost burn deviation vs forecast - notify infra-finance when edge spend delta > +8% daily.

Risks and open questions:
- Risk: Allowing temporary cost increase for latency reductions may create expectations with sales/customers. Product/CS comms needed if we plan to route critical tenants off edge. Action: Ellen to draft short playbook for CS by 2026-07-11.
- Open question: How aggressive should the eviction TTL be tuned for prefix cache under mixed workload? Priya to run TTL sweep experiments and report findings next sync.

Decisions made:
- Approve short pilot: +8% cache allocation in EU-west-edge for 48 hours (owner Diego).
- Approve driver alignment canary on 12 hosts in APAC-edge (owner Priya).
- Approve routing override to Dedicated for priority tenants during sustained latency incidents; on-call SRE to execute as part of incident runbook.

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Priya Kapoor: driver/kmod alignment patch + canary run (due 2026-07-09) [Linear RUN-498]
- Samir Patel: prewarm retry/backoff logic change + test (due 2026-07-10)
- Diego Morales: run prefix cache +8% pilot in EU-west-edge, collect 48hr signal (start 2026-07-08, end 2026-07-10)
- Morgan Lee (SRE): per-host queue depth telemetry dashboard and alert (due 2026-07-09)
- Ellen Wu: CS/PS playbook note for routing to Dedicated and customer-facing messaging (due 2026-07-11)
- Aisha Raman: follow-up sync and postmortem template if pilot fails (due 2026-07-12)

Notes / Misc:
- Observed a spurious autoscaler flapping event in eu-west-edge on 2026-07-04 03:00 UTC. Root cause likely related to bogus healthcheck results from network policy updates; investigating.
- Quick perf numbers to track: p50/p95 small-chat (target <80ms / <200ms), cache-hit target >40% for small-chat prefix workloads.

Next sync:
- Weekly follow-up scheduled 2026-07-13 10:00 PT. Agenda: pilot results, driver canary outcome, routing override runbook, cost delta reconciliation.

Appendix (short links and references):
- Linear tickets: RUN-482 (edge prewarm), RUN-498 (driver canary), RUN-512 (cache pilot)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/721 (latency-aware routing)
- Confluence: edge-fleet-telemetry (dashboard notes)
